questions.stem: Under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, who must maintain a record of a crew member's sea service?
options: Only the crew member
Only the authorized representative
Both the authorized representative and the crew member
Transport Canada, from the crew list
questions.explanation: CSA s. 93(1) puts the duty on the authorized representative and on every crew member. Each keeps a record, so you cannot leave it to the company.

questions.stem: A deckhand is discharged from a Canadian vessel. What must the authorized representative provide?
options: A certificate of discharge
A steering testimonial
A copy of the official log book
A new medical certificate
questions.explanation: CSA s. 92 requires a certificate of discharge, in the form the Minister specifies, when a crew member is discharged.

questions.stem: How long before the first exam must the discharge books, certificates of discharge and testimonials reach the examiner?
options: On the exam day
At least two days
At least one week
At least two weeks
questions.explanation: MPR s. 110(2) says at least two weeks before the first of the examinations the applicant seeks to take.

questions.stem: Which group of items must appear on a deck sea service testimonial?
options: Engine make, propulsive power and generator capacity
Official number, gross tonnage, voyage classification and sign-on and sign-off dates
Wages paid, next of kin and medical fitness
Chart numbers, tide tables used and compass error
questions.explanation: Schedule 4 lists the vessel's name, port of registry, official number, type, gross tonnage and voyage classification, with the dates, rank, days and drills. Engine details belong to the Schedule 5 engine testimonial.

questions.stem: Who signs a deck department testimonial to certify it is correct?
options: The applicant alone
The chief engineer
Any two crew members
The master or the authorized representative
questions.explanation: Schedule 4 item 12 requires the signature of the master or authorized representative. The chief engineer signs the engine testimonial, with the master or authorized representative.

questions.stem: What does the master declare in a steering testimonial?
options: The total hours the seafarer spent at the wheel
The distance the vessel steamed
The seafarer's days of leave
The number of pilotage transits made
questions.explanation: Schedule 3 carries the master's declaration that the seafarer stood regular watches for a stated total of hours at the wheel and is a competent wheelsman.

questions.stem: Which Canadian vessel must keep an official log book under the Marine Personnel Regulations?
options: A 12 GT water taxi on a sheltered waters voyage
A 40 GT crew boat on a near coastal voyage, Class 2
A 150 GT vessel on a near coastal voyage, Class 1
Every commercial vessel, whatever its size
questions.explanation: MPR s. 339(1) applies at 100 GT or more on an unlimited voyage, a near coastal voyage Class 1 or an international voyage other than an inland voyage. The two small vessels fail both the tonnage and the voyage tests.

questions.stem: How must an entry in the official log book be made and signed?
options: Weekly, signed by the owner
As soon as possible, dated, signed by the master and the chief mate or another crew member
At the end of the voyage, signed by the master alone
Within 30 days, signed by any officer
questions.explanation: MPR s. 339(4) and (5): as soon as possible, showing the date of the event and of the entry, signed by the master and also by the chief mate or another crew member.

questions.stem: How long does the authorized representative keep a completed official log book?
options: 12 months after the last entry
Two years after the voyage ends
Until the master leaves the vessel
Five years after completion, or until the registration changes if sooner
questions.explanation: MPR s. 340(5): the earlier of five years after the day the book was completed and the day the vessel's registration changes. Twelve months is the radio record period.

questions.stem: A 20 GT workboat does not have to keep an official log book. Where are its steering gear checks and emergency steering drills recorded?
options: Nowhere; no record is needed
In any log book
Only in the radio record
On the sea service testimonial
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 136(4) says the official log book if that Division applies to the vessel, or any log book if it does not.

questions.stem: What are the rules for the radio record?
options: Signed weekly by the master, kept five years
No initials needed, kept for the voyage only
Each entry initialled by the radio operator, kept at least 12 months after the last entry
Typed only, kept by Transport Canada
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 247(2) and (3): the operator making an entry initials it, and the record is kept not less than 12 months after the last entry.

questions.stem: A mate realises yesterday's log entry left out a grounding. What is the right thing to do?
options: Add a new, dated entry now recording the event
Rewrite yesterday's page so it looks complete
Leave it out, since the vessel was not damaged
Wait and mention it at the next inspection
questions.explanation: CSA s. 23 makes it an offence to make a false entry with intent to mislead or to wilfully omit an entry. A late entry shows both the date of the event and the date it was written (MPR s. 339(4)).
